subject: seeds::mk
statement: The selected position s is the first minimiser of |2b_s+1-N| over the five X bins, and the recorded s is the one used by every later stage.
evidence: paper p.8 ('This is the rule in seeds::mk'); no source
rationale: Validity is independent of which s is chosen: Lemma 2.4 holds for every non-initial column. Replace by the spec clause 's is any recorded element of {0..4}'. One line, no hypothesis needed.

subject: sumok
statement: sumok tests (2.11) in the residual direction and in directions perpendicular to the five unit-exponential columns.
rationale: (2.11) is quantified over all v, so testing any finite set of directions can only retain bins: soundness needs no property of the chosen directions. Delete the claim, keep 'any finite set of directions'.

subject: extend
statement: extend starts from [-1/2,1/2], intersects (2.14) for t=s (X) and t=0 (Y), omits divisors of magnitude <1e-6, and rejects only on strict disjointness.
rationale: Each clause is one-sided: omitting a divisor removes a constraint, +1e-7 on r and +1e-5 on endpoints enlarge. Certificate carries the two intervals; checker re-evaluates (2.14) with the stored margins.

subject: supdual
statement: supdual accepts proposals with |v_a|<=1e4 only (NaN-rejecting comparison) and evaluates (2.19) with 1.251*pi/N in place of 1.25*pi/N, adding a final support margin.
rationale: The stored v is exact rational data; 1.251>1.25 and the margin are conservative. Certificate carries v and the evaluated (2.19); checker recomputes in interval arithmetic.

subject: seeds::build, covout
statement: seeds::build visits every weakly increasing 5-bin X tuple and, for every first bin, every weakly increasing 4-bin Y tail; covout matches the shared bin and applies (2.8) second inequality and (2.14).
rationale: Enumeration completeness is the one part of Prop 2.10 not proved from the text. In the new pipeline it becomes structural (nested loops over the index box) and is certified by the certificate's declared index range: T3 implements, T2 checks range+count, T8 states 'the cover file contains every pair in the declared range'.

subject: testBucket
statement: testBucket succeeds only when the bound on (2.17) is below the lowered threshold fl((.032*112)^2)-1e-4.
rationale: The threshold is strictly below the nominal (NR)^2, so a success is conservative. Certificate carries the per-pair bound; checker compares against (NR)^2 exactly.

subject: block::setup, makeD, makeJ
statement: The stored frames G_B,G_C,K_B,K_C, the comparison block D and the linear map J equal the printed formulas (3.1),(3.5),(3.6),(3.15),(3.23) at the stored center.
evidence: paper pp.17-19 (entrywise coefficient formulas); A.4 p.59-60 table
rationale: §3.5 prints the nine seed and four angular coefficients entrywise, so this is checkable rather than asserted: checker recomputes J from (3.23) at the stored center and compares. Keep as a printed-formula match, not a code claim.

subject: eq
statement: eq stacks exactly the twenty real equations of (3.28): 16 flatness rows and 2x2 seed-sum rows.
rationale: The count 20=16+4 is arithmetic; the certificate's direction y has 20 coordinates, so the checker's dimension check enforces it.

subject: trial::pass
statement: trial::pass proposes directions by regularised solves and weight updates; it never excludes.
rationale: Cor 3.10 is quantified over y; the proposal method enters nowhere. Disposition: delete; replace by 'any finite list of directions may be tried'.

subject: trial::certificate
statement: trial::certificate is the only exclusion path: it rejects nonfinite y, requires max|y| in (1e-100,1e100), divides by max|y|, and uses the negative part of the flat weights as (3.29) requires.
rationale: This is the load-bearing half: (3.29) is positively homogeneous, so normalisation is free, and the max(0,max(-y_D)) term is exactly what the printed inequality needs. Certificate carries the normalised y and both sides of (3.29).

subject: Asearch::testA / Usearch::test
statement: Asearch::testA is the used Stage-A path; Usearch::test and the scalar routines supply no exclusions in this run.
rationale: A statement about which code is dead. In the new pipeline the certificate names the test that fired; dead paths cannot appear in a certificate. Record in T9's defect list (already code-audit F10).

subject: frame check
statement: The frame construction succeeds only if m>1.25 and the residuals exceed their floors; a failure leaves the seed unresolved, never excluded.
rationale: Lemma 3.1 needs only |S|<4 and a positive singular bound. Certificate carries m_B,m_C; checker re-derives them from the stored seed centre and asserts m>1.25.

subject: local::test, snapping
statement: local::test returns success only after a certified covercompute bound fits .103, and grows the radius to that bound; snapping only proposes a new centre, which must re-pass patch and the same covering computation.
rationale: The proof needs only 'the stored bound is certified and fits the target'. Certificate carries (bound, target, radius); checker compares. The snapping clause is a proposal mechanism and is deleted.

subject: buildH::patch
statement: A successful buildH::patch call certifies (4.4), (4.15) and a valid remainder constant C, hence produces Root data.
rationale: THE central S-claim. In the certificate reformulation it stops being a claim about a routine: the record stores P,T,M,C,n0,id,ort,hor,mnorm,froot and the checker verifies (4.4)+(4.15) directly, in interval arithmetic, from the stored data. Prop 4.5 then applies unchanged. This is the single largest reduction of the trust base.

subject: Candidate::prep
statement: Candidate::prep passes only with mag_j>.15, unit-chord discrepancy <1e-7, slack=max(0,z^2-sum+1e-5)+1e-10, q_d=slack/m_i+1e-8, invmag_j=1/(m_j-1e-6)+1e-9.
rationale: Lemma 4.8 needs (i) a nonnegative upper bound for z^2-sum(m_j-1)^2, (ii) a positive lower bound m_i, (iii) q_d<3.8. All three are stored numbers; checker re-derives them from z and the D entries.

subject: Candidate::delta
statement: Candidate::delta's rounded dephase and wrap determine integer lifts, and its atan2 proposal is accepted only through a unit-direction test |e((P0)_j)-Dnum/mnum|<1e-7.
rationale: (4.17) needs only that *some* fixed integer matrix N works, and any N does. The unit-direction test is a proposal check; delete the claim and keep 'N is any integer matrix with |N_ij|<=1 chosen by any rule'. The 2e-6 budget of (4.20) is then the only numerical input and it is CHECK-ed.

subject: covercompute::value
statement: covercompute::value computes supports (4.27)-(4.28), adds .0001 before dividing by pi, adds 1e-8 to d2, and returns s0=sqrt(nd+d2+(supp+.0001)/pi+1e-5).
rationale: (4.29) is a support inequality with an explicit margin; the stored centre carries the two supports and the checker evaluates (4.29) with them. Note the printed (4.29) has S_delta/pi inside the radical - the extraction needs care, and T8 should typeset it unambiguously.

subject: ell
statement: ell requires gap<=gamma-lambda_max(G) with gap>=1e-6, certifies U*(gamma I-G)^{-1}U by (4.37) at a finite trial solve z, and returns 100 as the failure sentinel.
rationale: (4.37) is an exact residual identity plus a gap division; the trial solve only proposes z. Certificate carries (gamma, z, bound); checker evaluates (4.37) in interval arithmetic. The sentinel-100 overloading must be replaced by a status flag (code-audit F4).

subject: spectralUpper
statement: spectralUpper bounds ||G|| by the smaller of (max abs row sum + 1e-10) and (||G^2||_F + 2e-7).
rationale: Both are exact matrix inequalities; the margins are one-sided. Checker recomputes both in interval arithmetic. In a switch to interval arithmetic the whole binary64 error budget disappears, so Lemma A.3 reduces to an elementary inequality.

subject: bootstrap
statement: bootstrap performs at most 30 updates of (4.38), inflating t by .00002 and the radius by 1e-6, with guards 0<=init<3 and C<20 and failure sentinel 10.
rationale: Prop 4.13 stops after any finite number of updates and only when the update decreases s; no convergence is claimed. Disposition: delete the count, keep the guard 'each update is applied only when it decreases the stored radius'.

subject: mapH, variants, canonicalMap
statement: mapH's two index arrays are genuine permutations, canonicalMap always finds at least one callback, and the signature choosing among maps need not be a canonical invariant.
rationale: Lemma 4.15 needs only the *existence* of an allowed Phi with a certified distance. Disposition: replace by 'the record stores the Phi it used'; the checker verifies Phi is a signed permutation (36-entry index map bijective) - one line.

subject: Atlas::find, Atlas::add
statement: Atlas::find returns computed norm + 1e-7 on success; Atlas::add grows the radius to at least r+d with 1e-8 added and compares to the cap with 2e-8 slack.
rationale: Lemma 4.15 is a triangle inequality; the only content is that d is an upper bound for the aligned distance. Certificate carries (Phi,N,d); checker recomputes the projected dephased difference in interval arithmetic.

subject: relationB::init
statement: relationB::init cuts at most .249 (direct-proposal path) and .23 (ordinary reuse); an inward cut only declines a relation.
rationale: Declining a relation only loses a coverage opportunity (Prop 5.7 keeps the parent in B or subdivides). One line; delete the numbers.

subject: relationB::eval
statement: relationB::eval performs at most 30 improvements of (5.16), accepts 0<=t<=2, returns sentinel 10 otherwise, and enlarges t by 2e-8 etc.
rationale: The sentinel and the count are irrelevant (Lemma 5.3 stops after any finite number of steps; enlargements are harmless). What must be checked is (5.17) at the stored t: the certificate carries t, the iterates and D-hat(t); checker re-evaluates (5.14)-(5.16) in interval arithmetic.

subject: rho search
statement: The threshold search starts at l=0, u=1.01a, makes 25 midpoint trials, replaces l only on a successful trial (5.18), and returns rho=max(0,l-1e-8) requiring rho>1e-7.
rationale: Lemma 5.4's proof uses exactly one stored trial value l; no monotonicity of D-hat is needed. Certificate carries (rho, l, D-hat(l)); checker verifies D-hat(l)<a-2e-7 and rho<=l.

subject: outside, corner, markRec
statement: outside subtracts 1e-8 inside each nonnegative part of (5.22) and compares with the inflated E^2; corner adds 1e-8; markRec keeps a branch while the partial sum <=(rho-5e-8)^2 and marks only whole base boxes.
rationale: Every clause is one-sided and geometric. The 'whole-box only' rule is the one that must be *proved* rather than checked (it is: (5.24) is a box maximum), so the certificate need only carry, per marked box, the box and the bound.

subject: assign, inverseTransform, addNear
statement: assign merges if r+l+2e-8<tau and grows to r+l+1e-8, else inserts Phi Q; inverseTransform and addNear are optional and a failure is ignored.
rationale: The merge is Lemma 5.6's triangle inequality with a stored l; the optional steps are irrelevant (a later failure cannot undo an assignment). Split: merge=CHECK, optional steps=DELETE.

subject: batch writer
statement: Batches hold at most 256 records, write the radius as the common cap tau, use a temporary file and atomic rename, and a count marker; a count marker alone is not a certificate.
rationale: This is a finite-execution condition, not mathematics: (5.27) does the work. Promote into Theorem 7.1 as 'every emitted batch is included and its record set is exactly the set of indices it claims'.

subject: Layer::test
statement: Layer::test applies (6.7), then (6.12), then (6.11) for proposed directions, each normalised by its maximum entry, which must lie in (1e-100,1e100).
rationale: All three are necessary conditions quantified over y, so proposals are free. Certificate carries the retained/excluded bins with the direction and both sides of the inequality that fired.

subject: single::support, graph::joint
statement: single::support forms J*y and the real companion sums with a zero vector-displacement coefficient array first; graph::joint then adds the edge derivatives, and accumulates both -(B^t)*y_t before taking the tangent norm.
rationale: This ordering is what makes (6.22) a max of a *pure* single-vector remainder, which is needed for (6.23) to be necessary. In the checker, (6.23) is evaluated as printed; the ordering claim then becomes a statement about the printed formula, not about code.

subject: cluster
statement: cluster runs at most two Lloyd-like iterations with the last iteration not moving centres, recomputes radii from the final assignment, caps at 2048 centres, requires |v_j|<=2 and 0<=s<.1, and uses the candidate threshold (.042-1.11w)^2.
rationale: Lemma 6.4 is a covering statement about the *final* assignment: 'radius >= ||h||+X_M'. Certificate carries (v,m,s) per ball and the assignment; checker recomputes ||h|| per assigned bin. The heuristic and the threshold can be deleted. NOTE: the threshold formula is degenerate for M<26 (code-audit F2) - deleting it is the fix.

subject: graph::exist (mode 1)
statement: The mode-1 search enumerates least vertices, deletes the root from both pools when the first-clique target is six, prunes with an auxiliary six-clique test on the second pool, caps at 5e6 steps and sets a persistent give-up flag.
rationale: This is the only lemma in the paper whose subject is an algorithm. Disposition: formalise the search as a function on finite graphs with the spec 'exist=false => (6.24) is infeasible' (about 30 lines of Lean over a bitset model), and cross-check T3's implementation against it on samples. A witness-based alternative is T2 P4.4's hard sub-problem.

subject: negative
statement: Stage C reports negative only on an empty completed bin layer or a completed negative graph search; caps, clustering failures and surviving possibilities are unresolved.
rationale: The 'no negative unless ...' implication is the certificate's own type discipline; in the new pipeline it is enforced by the certificate format (a negative record must carry its witness). Promote the *execution* half into Theorem 7.1's hypothesis and the *format* half into T2's cert-format.

subject: platform and compiler
statement: The run used the stated builds (g++ 13.3.0, -O3 -march=native -ffp-contract=off), binary64 round-to-nearest with no FTZ/DAZ, and in covout both pow(...,2) calls were lowered to binary64 multiplications.
rationale: An arithmetic-model premise. It disappears if the checker evaluates certificates in exact/interval arithmetic: proposals may use any float arithmetic because their accuracy is never assumed. Recommend: delete Section 7.1's model conditions and replace A.1-A.3 by interval-arithmetic primitives. The pow-lowering observation is a nice touch but belongs to the old certificate.

subject: terminal conditions
statement: The five terminal conditions (builds+cover complete; four A exits 0 with empty bad files; two B exits 0 with zero-count bad files; each initial C batch processed once with consistent counts; fallback covers every initial failure and the four final C shards partition the fallback records).
rationale: Exactly what Theorem 7.1 should state as its finite-execution hypothesis. In the new pipeline the analogue is 'the checker accepts the certificate file', which is one condition instead of five.

subject: arithmetic model
statement: A dot product of length m<=2000 satisfies (A.3) with gamma_m=2.1e-16(m+1); power sums and norms satisfy (A.4).
rationale: A statement about an arithmetic model, true of binary64 but needing a 20-page propagation. Under interval arithmetic it is replaced by exact bounds; keep only if the checker is float-based.

subject: expair
statement: For |x|<=16, expair is within 2e-14 of e(x) in complex modulus, and eps_exp=6e-14 suffices in all uses.
rationale: Same: an implementation claim. Its second half (|pi-hat - pi| < 1.225418e-16 by Machin plus exact rational arithmetic, (A.8)-(A.9)) is M and pleasantly checkable - keep that, drop the polynomial.

subject: spectralUpper
statement: spectralUpper returns an upper bound for ||G|| for exact symmetric stored G with k<=10 and |G_ij|<=10.
rationale: See S-Root-6; identical disposition.

subject: the run
rationale: Observed data about an execution whose archive is not in the packet. Internally consistent (all sums reproduce), but not a certificate. In the new paper it is replaced by the checker's accepted record count; keep as a historical table with the 'not verified here' tag.

subject: hashes
statement: SHA-256 digests of eight principal data files.
rationale: Unverifiable without the archive; drop from the new paper or move to a data-availability statement.
